I have a very similar setup - the only difference is that I have 7900 XTX.

I think this is a driver issue on AMD's end.

I have recently been learning shader programming and playing with emission and post-processing settings.

I have the same random crashes on my setup as well, it's very random. Sometimes it takes 5 seconds, sometimes nothing happens for about 2 hours. It crashes even in the editor.

I noticed that right before it crashes, my GPU actually hangs / stops responding entirely and then Windows restarts the graphics drivers which actually triggers the crash.

I tried building the latest version of the engine and it still crashes. Recently I have tried downgrading my GPU drivers to see if it's the recent drivers that's causing it. After downgrading my GPU drivers to 24.05.01 solved the crashes (and, I get much higher performance as well, almost double what I used to get).

This is not a viable solution though, I don't think people would start downgrading their drivers just to be able to play one game. And I doubt AMD will work on a fix on their end, at least not any time soon.

- Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/71929.

> My game crashes on a testers PC after running for 5-10 minutes.

Does the game crash after a while if limited to a low framerate (e.g. using the `--max-fps 20` command line argument)?

Do other demanding games and benchmarks crash on the same machine?

Does the crash persist if using `--rendering-driver d3d12` to run the project (or switching the rendering driver for `windows` to `d3d12` in the Project Settings)?

Hello there! I am sure that this issue is on AMD's end. Many people have reported issues with AMD GPU's, some with GPUs such as the RX 6600 or RX 7900. Mostly, they came & asked us in the discord server. For more info, I suggest that you check out the discord server.

Heard back from my tester considering your questions @Calinou, here's the answers:

Does the game crash after a while if limited to a low framerate (e.g. using the `--max-fps 20` command line argument)?
-> no crash occurred during a ~30 minute playsession using only the --max-fps 20  argument

Do other demanding games and benchmarks crash on the same machine?
-> no other demanding games have caused any crashes(battlefield 6, path of exile 2, expedition 33)

Does the crash persist if using `--rendering-driver d3d12` to run the project (or switching the rendering driver for `windows` to `d3d12` in the Project Settings)?
-> no crash occured during a ~30 minute playsession using only the --rendering-driver d3d12 argument. However initial load time spiked up from 2-3 seconds to 20-25 seconds. this only happened during the first game launch, probably for some sort of game set up.

Be aware that the crash has been somewhat elusive during testing. Typically crashing within 5-15 minutes of playtime but sometimes not at all.

> -> no crash occurred during a ~30 minute playsession using only the --max-fps 20 argument

This makes me think the crash is related to either a race condition in Vulkan code (therefore timing-sensitive), or the GPU becomes unstable at high loads. That said, if the user has been able to run demanding games on it without a FPS limit (other than V-Sync), GPU unstability at high loads is probably not the issue.

> However initial load time spiked up from 2-3 seconds to 20-25 seconds. this only happened during the first game launch, probably for some sort of game set up.

This is what https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102552 aims to address (as long as it's enabled during export, and the export is performed from a Windows machine).

Unfortunately, it still crashes after a while in a 4.5 build for both of my testers with Radeon RX 7900 XT cards.
The Vulkan crashlogs still look the same. Got some new info from the d3d12 logs though.
The errors at first point to places in the code where I update an ImageTexture with an Image: renderTexture.Update(renderImage);
The following errors occur:
```
ERROR: Map failed with error 0x887a0005.
ERROR: Parameter "data_ptr" is null.
```
After that it's back to the errors from my previous comment (without call stack).
Full crashlog here:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MfSBKRM5-dLO7H9gdqE_MsF9jsYWQ9bH/view?usp=sharing

That's just for one tester though, for the other one it just crashes with signal 11 and no further info.
